known.title: The repair write uses `gh api -f body=@<body-file>`, but `-f` sends the literal text `@<path>` and does not read the file.
known.locator: Research, Fix 1 shape bullet (line 13); Steps, row 1 step_repair (line 23)
known.summary: The Fix 1 shape makes `editIssueBodyIfUnchanged` send the repaired body of a `finished` plan with `gh api --method PATCH repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/<n> -f body=@<body-file>` instead of `gh issue edit --body-file`, and it says that `-f body=@<body-file>` reads the value from the temporary body file. The gh manual (https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_api) says that `-f/--raw-field` values add "static string parameters to the request payload". Only the `-F/--field` flag reads a file: "if the value starts with `@`, the rest of the value is interpreted as a filename to read the value from". So `-f` sends the literal text `@<path>` as the new body. At repo_ref, `withBodyFile` (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:539-560) gives an absolute path under the state directory, and `runGh` (plan.mjs:305-314) calls `spawnSync` with an argv array and no shell, so nothing expands the value. Effect: the repair replaces the body of the closed plan with one path line. The record loses its v3 marker, so `readPlanIssue` (plan.mjs:84, 518) refuses it as unreadable and `archive` can never verify the plan. The public issue also shows a machine path, which the contract forbids (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md:103-104). The read-back at plan.mjs:576-577 fails only after GitHub stored the wrong body. A gh stub in the CLI suite cannot prove the claim, because the stub parses the arguments itself. A local check with gh 2.102.0: `gh api -X GET search/issues -f q=@q.txt --verbose` requests `q=%40q.txt`, and `-F q=@q.txt` sends the content of the file. Fix: keep `gh issue edit --body-file` (plan.mjs:566), or use `-F body=@<body-file>`.

known.title: The new exported helper breaks the self-test that pins the closed export list of plan.mjs, and no step changes that self-test.
known.locator: Research, Fix 2 shape bullet (line 14); Steps, row 2 edit_guard (line 24); Acceptance, row A3 (line 35)
known.summary: The Fix 2 shape adds a new exported function `stepStatusRegressions(before, after)` to plan.mjs, so that `scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs` can import it. At repo_ref, `plugins/plan-lifecycle/test/selftest.mjs:27-29` imports plan.mjs and asserts that `Object.keys(planCli).sort()` deep-equals `['checkPlan', 'machinePathCitations']`, with the message "plan.mjs must expose only the closed plan CLI API". A module namespace object has one enumerable key for each export (MDN, https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/import: "A module namespace object is an object that describes all exports from a module" and "All keys are enumerable"). So the new export makes the self-test fail. No step changes `plugins/plan-lifecycle/test/selftest.mjs`: rows 2 and 3 change only plan.mjs, plan-cli.mjs, and the gh stub, and row 5 only runs the gate. Research (line 15) names the self-test only as a manifest and contract check. Effect: A3 (`node plugins/plan-lifecycle/test/selftest.mjs`) fails, and A4 and the row 5 Done when fail too, because the plugin gate runs the self-test (`scripts/ci.mjs:548-551`). A local check with Node 24.22.1 on a copy of plan.mjs at repo_ref with one more export: the same `assert.deepEqual` fails with that message. Fix: keep the comparison inside `editPlan` and test it through the CLI, or add a step that widens the closed export list in the self-test on purpose.

known.title: The plan leaves `docs/PLAN.md` and the workspace template unchanged, but both state the closed-plan step rule and the `edit` refusal list that the plan changes.
known.locator: Research, Contract text bullet (line 16); Steps, row 4 contract_docs, Task and Files cells (line 26)
known.summary: The Research bullet says that `docs/PLAN.md` and the workspace template only say that `step` checks the plan state and dependencies and leave the closed-plan rule to the contract, so neither file changes. Row 4 drops both files from its Files cell. At repo_ref, both files own the same rule in their own words: `docs/PLAN.md:127-130` and `plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-workspace/references/plan-md-template.md:131-134` say "Once that merge closes the issue as completed, the derived state is `finished` and step mutation is no longer legal." Both also give the full list of `edit` refusals (`docs/PLAN.md:257-260`, template lines 261-264), which the new regression refusal extends. The plan changes the rule in plan.mjs:905 and in `plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md:138-140`. `plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/AGENTS.md:58-78` puts issue write preconditions in the synchronized surface and says to synchronize the template and `docs/PLAN.md` when any part changes. `scripts/tests/plan-skill-phases.mjs:679-686` only compares `docs/PLAN.md` with the template fence, so A2 passes when neither file changes. `plan-workspace` copies the template fence into each consumer `docs/PLAN.md` (`plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-workspace/SKILL.md:130-132`). Effect: the repository standard and the shipped template keep saying that a finished plan takes no step mutation, while the CLI and the contract allow the terminal repair. A closed plan is the normal state after the closing merge (GitHub docs, https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue: "When you merge a linked pull request into the default branch of a repository, its linked issue is automatically closed."), so the stale rule covers exactly the case that the plan repairs. Fix: keep both files in row 4 and change the same sentences there.

known.title: No step runs the content-hash backfill that the plan-lifecycle skills node requires after a skill meaning change, so the plugin gate fails on hash drift.
known.locator: Steps, row 5 gate, Task cell (line 27); Acceptance, row A4 (line 36)
known.summary: Row 5 now only runs the plugin gate, and no other step re-syncs the skill content hashes. Row 4 changes `plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md` and `plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/SKILL.md`. At repo_ref, the `<constraint>` block at `plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/AGENTS.md:24-33` says: "After changing a skill's meaning, run `node scripts/skills/content-hash.mjs --backfill plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills`." The hash covers the SKILL.md body and every `references/*.md` file of the skill (`scripts/skills/content-hash.mjs:4-5` and `hashSkill` at 73-88), and `plan-manager/SKILL.md:7-8` stores `updated` and `content_hash`. The plugin gate runs `content-hash.mjs --check-only` and fails on drift (`scripts/ci.mjs:578-580`). A local check on a snapshot of repo_ref: one sentence appended to plan-contract.md makes `node scripts/skills/content-hash.mjs --check-only plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills` print `would-bump productivity/plan-manager (content changed)` and exit 1. Effect: the instruction-file rule is left out of the Steps, and the row 5 Done when (`node scripts/ci.mjs --plugin plan-lifecycle` exit 0) and A4 cannot pass as planned. Fix: put the backfill back into row 5 before the gate.
